rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C: ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices (software that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for vacant units) to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units. A tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action for violations.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of algorithmic rent-setting devices; enforceable by civil action by a tenant or the City Attorney

coverage.summary: Applies to residential units in San Francisco; no exemptions stated in the document.

rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.
rules.review_note: Document is an official Rent Board news notice, not the ordinance text. The definition is described as a device that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rent for vacant units. Penalties are not stated beyond civil action.

result.doc_summary: Rent Board news item (Oct. 16, 2024) announcing that Section 37.10C of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance took effect on October 14, 2024. It bans the sale or use of algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to set rents or manage occupancy for residential units, and allows tenants or the City Attorney to sue.
